activities.label: Product rule basics
activities.title: Product rule model
activities.body: Read the model and focus on the two-term structure. Then answer the check from memory.

essentialIdeas: The product rule says to differentiate a product by adding two terms: first derivative times second function, plus first function times second derivative.

activities.label: Explain the product rule
activities.title: Product rule in your words
activities.body: Explain the rule from memory in plain language. Keep it to one short paragraph.
activities.concept: Product rule
activities.correctAnswer: For a product of two functions, differentiate each part one at a time and add the two results: f'g + fg'.
activities.feedback: A complete answer names both terms and shows that each factor gets differentiated once. A common gap is leaving out one term or treating it like a simple power rule.

activities.label: Fix the product rule
activities.title: Repair the product rule
activities.body: Use the feedback to correct your explanation. Give one corrected version.
activities.misconceptionSummary: Product rule means multiply derivatives straight across instead of making two terms.
activities.concept: Product rule
activities.correctAnswer: The product rule is f'g + fg', not f'g'.
activities.feedback: The repair should separate the two terms and show that both factors matter. If you only wrote one derivative product, the missing part is the second term.

activities.label: Chain rule basics
activities.title: Chain rule model
activities.body: Read the model and look for the outside and inside parts. Then answer the check from memory.

essentialIdeas: The chain rule says to differentiate a composite by multiplying the outside derivative by the inside derivative.

activities.label: Explain the chain rule
activities.title: Chain rule in your words
activities.body: Explain the rule from memory in plain language. Keep it focused on how the two parts connect.
activities.concept: Chain rule
activities.correctAnswer: For a composite function, differentiate the outside function and multiply by the derivative of the inside function.
activities.feedback: A complete answer shows the outside inside connection and the multiply by the inside derivative step. A common gap is differentiating only the outside part.

activities.label: Choose the chain rule
activities.title: Identify the chain rule
activities.body: Pick the derivative rule that fits this situation. Choose one answer.
activities.concept: Chain rule
choices: Differentiate the outside expression, then multiply by the derivative of the inside.
Differentiate each factor and add the results.
Differentiate only the outermost symbol and stop.
activities.correctAnswer: Differentiate the outside expression, then multiply by the derivative of the inside.
activities.feedback: That choice matches a composite function, where the inside derivative must be included. The other options either mix in the product rule or leave out part of the chain rule.
